page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 26.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 6.5 GB per core. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate that the n1-highmem-4 delivers modest compute performance. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU score is 1109.89 and the multi-core score is 2914.17, both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Geekbench testing shows a single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 2032.0, placing it in the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 162.39 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Redis SET operations achieve 2.75 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.82 GB/sec.

Given its older Intel Xeon architecture and lower benchmark scores relative to modern hardware, the n1-highmem-4 offers a resource profile suited for legacy workloads requiring higher memory density without intensive compute demands. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPUs limits its utility for high-performance databases or machine learning training. It is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, small database instances, and basic web serving.
